title: NWP500 external control plan, protocol 0
description: A plan tells the integration's external control feature what state the heater should be in, and when. The feature programs it into the heater's reservation list. Top-level keys are attributes of the intent entity. Rules that span documents or depend on the device (superseded plans, bounds, allowed modes, the horizon and the entry budget) are checked by the feature and are listed in docs/external-control-spec.md.

protocol.description: Protocol version. A major version the feature does not support rejects the document (unsupported_protocol).

intent_id.description: Unique per plan. The intent entity's state must change on every new plan; use this.

issued_at.description: When the scheduler made the plan. An older document never replaces a newer one (superseded).

segments.description: The timeline, in strictly increasing order of start. Each segment holds until the next segment's start; the last holds until a new plan. An empty list stops the plan: every programmed entry is withdrawn and the heater keeps its state.

grants.description: Surplus grants: permission to raise the setpoint while surplus power is available and the compressor is already running.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 with a UTC offset. Naive timestamps are rejected. Truncated to the minute.

mode_name.description: vacation and power_off are never accepted: reservations do not run in either, so the heater would stay off. Use setpoint "min" instead.

id.description: Unique in the document, across segments and grants.

setpoint.description: The lowest setpoint the feature will write (setpoint_min). Effectively off: it applies inside TOU windows, and the next segment's entry restores normal operation.

mode.description: Required on the first segment. A later segment that omits it keeps the previous segment's mode.

id.description: Unique in the document, across segments and grants.

end.description: Must be later than start after truncation, or the grant alone is rejected (invalid_window).
